subject.title: [Feature]: Cron job output routing — hard-coded destination for job results (file, channel, session)

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class cron output-target contract, and which target types, fallback/status semantics, and security boundaries should be included in the first version?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix adds public cron config/protocol surface plus scheduler-owned file writes, channel sends, and invisible session injection that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design unified output targets
options.body: Add one explicit cron output-target contract for file, channel, and session targets with strict safety, authorization, fallback, status, docs, and tests.

options.title: Split narrower trackers
options.body: Keep this as the umbrella and implement smaller approved slices such as `cron.defaults.delivery` or session delivery only after their APIs are decided.

options.title: Keep prompt-owned routing
options.body: Decline framework-owned output routing for now and document prompt/message-tool patterns plus the current delivery modes as the supported path.

recommendation.title: Design unified output targets
recommendation.body: Add one explicit cron output-target contract for file, channel, and session targets with strict safety, authorization, fallback, status, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from cron delivery history, related ClawSweeper reviews, and maintainer-facing product boundary decisions.
